title: Kinds of piece with no rule yet

steps.path: Library, Pages, Resume — when a list is empty
steps.headline: Which look should an empty list or empty area use, everywhere?
steps.notice: The app has four different looks for "nothing here yet". Pick the one to use in all of them.

variants.label: Plain text + link
variants.summary: One grey line and a small outlined button (Library).

variants.label: Card + one button
variants.summary: A short explanation and one full-width filled button (Pages).

variants.label: Title + hint
variants.summary: A bold line and a grey hint, no button (Pages, nothing picked).

variants.label: One grey line
variants.summary: Only a grey sentence in the middle (Resume, nothing picked).

steps.risk: Different jobs may deserve different answers, e.g. card for first-time, one line for nothing picked. Choosing 'Other' and saying so is fine.

steps.headline: Should quick pop-up pickers get a title and ✕ like other popups?
steps.notice: The switcher has a search box and "Esc" instead of a title and ✕. The skills drawer, filters and tag notes are similar.

options.label: Quick pickers stay light
pros: Fast to use; search box is the header.
Closes on Esc or a click outside.
cons: A few popups lack ✕ while every other popup has one.

options.label: Every popup gets a title and ✕
pros: A ✕ is obvious on touch screens.
cons: A title above a search box takes room and slows the picker.

steps.headline: Should one of the five sign-in choices be the main (filled) one?
steps.notice: All five are equal outlined pills. The guide says one filled button per view.

options.label: Keep five equal choices
pros: No choice is pushed on anyone.
Fits people using a key or a local model.
cons: Breaks "one filled button"; nothing stands out.

options.label: Fill the subscription sign-in
pros: Points most people to the easy path.
cons: Favours one company's sign-in over the others.

options.label: Sign-in accounts filled, other ways as small links
cons: Hides the local-model and key paths a little.

steps.headline: Should the smallest text (hints, dates, counts) grow from 10px to 11px?
steps.changed: Every 10px hint, date and caption in the app becomes 11px. Nothing else changes.
steps.notice: Text under settings titles is a little bigger and easier to read; some rows are a few pixels taller.
steps.risk: About 460 places grow, so tight spots (status bar, chips, cards) may wrap or crowd; those would be checked before shipping.

steps.headline: Same question on Remote Access: keep 10px, or 11px?
steps.changed: The hint lines and small labels here grow from 10px to 11px.
steps.notice: Hints under Password and Tailscale are easier to read; the popup is a little longer.
steps.risk: Busy screens get a little denser to scroll.

steps.headline: Should a bar's number be normal grey text, with only the bar carrying colour?
steps.changed: Today the percentages beside usage bars are coloured text: green 34%, amber 12% (Cloud providers, the usage card, the status bar). New rule: the bar keeps its colour; the number is the normal grey.
steps.notice: Numbers become easier to read on pale themes; the colour still shows how full a bar is.

steps.headline: Should the small tag beside a title ("Optional", "Stopped") be the same tinted pill as a status?
steps.changed: Today these are outlined boxes, plain grey words, or capitals. New rule: one small tinted pill in normal case, the same as "Installed".
steps.notice: Backups' "Optional" and the Local engine's "Stopped" would look like the Installed pill.

steps.headline: Should status-bar chips use normal case, with only a real problem coloured as a tinted pill?
steps.changed: Today chips mix capitals (NORMAL, PERMISSION UNKNOWN), coloured values and dots. New rule: normal case and normal text colour; a problem shows as a tinted pill.
steps.notice: The status bar looks calmer; "Permission unknown" no longer shouts in red capitals.

steps.surface: Lists of things to switch on
steps.headline: Should a tick-box list (Customize status bar, bug-report options) use a settings-style row, tick box on the left?
steps.changed: Today these are hand-built small tick boxes with loose spacing. New rule: each item is a boxed row like a setting; the whole row is tappable; the tick box sits on the left.
steps.notice: Same look as the "I understand" line you picked earlier.

steps.headline: Should a slider have its label above it, the value at the right of the label, and the slider full width below?
steps.changed: Today (Theme editor) sliders sit beside their labels and don't line up. New rule follows your "wide controls go below" choice.
steps.notice: Sliders line up in one column.

steps.headline: Should an error or notice that appears in the chat use the same tinted notice box, with its buttons inside at the right?
steps.changed: Today chat errors (sign-in expired, out of credit, plan limit) are red text or a strip with a bare "Details" link.
steps.notice: The same box you picked for Backup & Sync; "Upgrade plan" and "Details" become real buttons inside it.

steps.headline: Should every icon-only button show its name when hovered, and be used only for things people already know?
steps.changed: Today many icon buttons (grid/list, pin, star, pencil) have no name.
steps.notice: Nothing changes visibly until you hover.

steps.headline: Should a disabled main button say why, in one grey line beside or under it?
steps.changed: Today a greyed-out button (OpenRouter's key box, unavailable Resume) gives no reason.
steps.notice: A short grey line appears under such buttons.

steps.surface: Surfaces that stay as they are
steps.headline: Should games, code diffs, file viewers, charts, the message box and chat bubbles stay exempt for now?
steps.changed: Like tool cards, permission prompts and the terminal, they are not covered by the guide yet, and no new screen should copy them.
steps.notice: The guide lists them as "not final"; nothing changes on screen.
